title: The base-branch triage loader swallows a parse error, the shape DEC-213 ruled against
description:
gate.py run(): the base-branch triage file (testing/survivors.json, from policy assurance.triage_file) is read with json.loads(base_t) if base_t.strip() else {}, inside a try/except ValueError that returns {}. An unparseable triage file at the base ref therefore reads as no triage entries, which is the fail-open shape DEC-213 closed for the quarantine and probation files.

This task does not decide whether DEC-213 extends to it: DEC-213 names only the quarantine and probation files, so opum-doc decides whether the ruling reaches the triage file. Filed at the leader instruction on 2026-10-20, To Do and unclaimed, off the plan.

Note for whoever picks it up: a missing file and an existing unparseable one can be told apart only by asking git for presence first, the way _load_list_at now does for the base-ref state files.
finalSummary: Resolved by DEC-213 (a1), 2026-10-20 at 13:31Z, read from opum-doc's .quest/planning.json at dev: DEC-213 does NOT extend to the base-branch triage loader, because that swallow fails toward STRICT, not open. With an unparseable base, base_triage becomes {}, so every entry counts as self-added, and at R4+ a self-added entry counts only with a listed approver: the swallow refuses more entries and removes no protection. What remains is a confusing message rather than a hole, and under the 2026-10-05 ruling against a hardening spiral that does not justify a change on its own. No code change is made. If this loader is touched for another reason, a one-line comment at the except saying that it fails toward strict and why is permitted, optional, and uses no test slot.
